content.title: Bas Mazagran: A Contextual Approach to Coastal Housing
summary: Rising on the Mostaganem coastline, Bas Mazagran reimagines collective living through seven monolithic structural blocks. The master plan seamlessly integrates 200 high-accessibility residences and 38 premium homes, supported by active commercial storefronts designed to anchor the developing streetscape.

Bridging the urban fabric and the coastal fringe, Bas Mazagran optimizes vertical density through its structural massing, facade articulation, and active public ground design, now advancing into its definitive delivery phase.
description: The architectural layout distributes 238 residences across seven geometrically aligned blocks, prioritizing optimal solar orientation, cross-ventilation, and an efficient configuration of four apartments per structural core.

Currently advancing through its final phase, site operations are focused on the fine-tuning of secondary architectural works, advanced thermal building envelopes, integrated technical infrastructure, and the landscaping of dedicated pedestrian arteries.

faq.question: What is 200 Assisted Housing and 38 Free Promotional Housing Units?
faq.answer: Bas Mazagran is a coastal urban master plan composed of seven mid-rise residential blocks that unify inclusive social housing, private premium real estate, and pedestrian-centric commerce.

faq.question: What was the project scope?
faq.answer: The project encompasses the spatial and structural execution of 238 distinct apartments across seven blocks, maintaining a highly efficient spatial ratio of four residences per landing.

faq.question: Who led the delivery?
faq.answer: The architectural realization and state infrastructure integration are spearheaded by OPGI, ensuring a balance between regional development and high-density urban design.

faq.question: What makes the project notable?
faq.answer: Bridging the urban fabric and the coastal fringe, Bas Mazagran optimizes vertical density through its structural massing, facade articulation, and active public ground design, now advancing into its definitive delivery phase.
